Subject: RE: Major latency spike impacting checkout (3/20) — initial findings and mitigation

Team / Sam — initial triage update from the on-call and platform team:

Summary of what happened (short):
- Between 06:25–07:10 PT we observed a sudden increase in KV cache miss amplification for the Redwood-verified caching layer due to a shift in request prefix distribution from Crestline's load tests. This caused a sharp increase in model forward passes per request and a temporary CPU/GPU scheduling backlog on our dedicated pool nodes serving their traffic.
- Error mode: timeouts surfaced at the gateway when the request queue exceeded the per-route concurrency threshold, triggering 502s for a small fraction (~3.8%) of requests.

Immediate mitigations performed (completed by 11:40 PT):
1) Increased per-route concurrency cap for text-generation/redwood-large-v2 for Crestline's dedicated pool (temporary override).
2) Forced prefix-mapping warmup by replaying cached prefixes from last known-good window (reduced KV misses).
3) Shifted 20% of Crestline traffic to a warmed spillover pool to reduce queuing pressure.

Result: 95/99 latency improved to within SLO for the majority of traffic; error rate reduced from 3.8% to 0.6% within one hour.

Owners / next steps for RCA (deliverable in 48h):
- Marissa Cole (Eng, Owner): collect traces, kernel-level metrics, scheduler logs, and quantify root cause contribution percentages.
- Laura Bennett (Infra): analyze capacity/placement decisions and autoscaler signals.
- Rachel Kim (Customer lead): prepare exec-facing RCA and customer communications.
- Karthik Iyer (Sales): coordinate readout scheduling and business impact notes.

Attachments: crestline_rca_draft.pdf (engineering draft), query_traces_mar20-22.zip (traces)

I'll circulate a formal RCA doc and a remediation runbook within 48 hours. If you want earlier details for the readout, flag them and we'll prioritize.

-Marissa
Sr. Manager, Platform Engineering | Redwood Inference

Subject: Crestline RCA (executive summary) and remediation commitments

Sam / Amy — attaching the exec summary of the RCA we discussed and the remediation commitments to prevent recurrence. Short highlights below: 

- Root cause (summary): sudden change in request prefix distribution led to cache-miss amplification, exposing scheduler contention on Dedicated pool nodes; secondary contributor was a conservative per-route concurrency cap that tripped gateways when queueing spiked.
- Immediate outcome: temporary capacity and cache-warmup mitigations restored SLOs within 1 hour.
- Remediation plan (timeline):
  * Short-term (0–7 days): implement automatic prefix-warmup during traffic surges; adjust per-route concurrency policies to allow controlled burst capacity.
  * Mid-term (2–4 weeks): scheduler tuning to improve queue headroom and smarter spillover thresholds; add a synthetic prefix-warmup run in deployment pipelines.
  * Long-term (2–3 months): adaptive routing policy improvements and a model-variant fallback for extremely high tail cases.

We committed the formal RCA and remediation runbook (attached) and will follow up with a technical deep-dive session for Crestline SREs next week.

Requested customer asks: please confirm the 15:00 PT readout on 3/20 is helpful — we can also expand to include Crestline engineering.

Attachments: crestline_rca_draft.pdf, remediation_runbook.md

Thanks again for patience; we take this seriously and will report progress on the remediation milestones.

Rachel Kim
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
